newsitem.title: UK: Polar explorer to take politicians to Antarctic.
newsitem.headline: Polar explorer to take politicians to Antarctic.

text.p: British explorer Robert Swan, the only person to have walked to both North and South Poles, said on Wednesday he plans a crusade to bring politicians to the Antarctic to show them the impact of global warming.
Swan has bought a 120-foot (36-metre) sailing yacht in which he proposes over the next five years to take young people and opinion formers to the area.

"I want to take politicians, young people, business people, celebrities if necessary, down to the Antarctic to see what I have seen," Swan told reporters. "We are genuinely, without a shadow of a doubt, melting certain areas of the Antarctic."

Swan, who is a Special Envoy to the Director General of the United Nations Education, Scientific, and Cultural Organisation (UNESCO), was speaking after appearing at a news conference held by Britain's minority Liberal Democrat Party.
Although not a party member, he backed new party proposals for a carbon tax to reduce Britain's carbon dioxide emissions.

He said he had personally felt the impact of the disappearance of the ozone layer above the two poles. His eyesight had suffered as his eyes had changed colour due to the effect of ultraviolet rays, he said.

He almost died in 1989 when the Arctic Ocean melted beneath him in April in an area where melting was not due to occur until August, and he had sailed around islands in the Antarctic which used to be impossible to circumnavigate.
Swan will give further details of his five million pound ($8.3 million), five-year plan, for which he has received sponsorship from a range of organisations, at a news conference in London on Friday.
